1. The SRG flow equations provide an efficient and robust way to decouple low- and high-energy matrix element of nuclear interactions, leading to dramatic improvement in variational calculations of few-body nuclear systems.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of new techniques to the study of the structure of few-nucleon systems, with particular emphasis on those techniques that can be applied to systems of increasing complexity.

the development and implementation of new nuclear Hamiltonians that are systematically improved in a way that preserves their essential features, and that provide the basis for a new generation of nuclear structure calculations.
the application of RG methods to the nuclear many-body problem.

the renormalization group method, in particular the similarity renormalization group, has become a very powerful tool in nuclear physics.

the SRG flow equation is an efficient tool to construct NN potentials and to study the evolution of nuclear structure properties.
